topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes for the hallmarks of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This opening subtopic introduces the lecture's conceptual framework, historical background, and key learning outcomes regarding the hallmarks of cancer.

topics.label: Growth signal autonomy and proliferative signaling pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how cancer cells achieve sustained proliferation through genetic mutations that constitutively activate growth-promoting pathways such as Wnt/beta-catenin and receptor tyrosine kinases.

topics.label: Blocks to terminal differentiation in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how cancers in both the hematopoietic system and the intestinal epithelium arrest maturation to maintain an undifferentiated, proliferative state.

topics.label: Resistance to apoptosis through p53 and Bcl-2 regulation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the mechanisms by which cancer cells evade programmed cell death through disruptions in the balance between pro- and anti-apoptotic proteins regulated by p53.

topics.label: Replicative immortality, senescence bypass, and cellular stress checkpoints
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how cancer cells achieve unlimited replicative potential by maintaining telomeres and overcoming p53-mediated senescence and DNA damage arrest checkpoints.

topics.label: Metabolic rewiring and oncometabolites in cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how tumor cells alter cellular bioenergetics through aerobic glycolysis and Krebs cycle mutations that produce oncometabolites to drive cancer progression and epigenetic remodeling.

topics.label: Induction of tumor angiogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how growing tumors overcome hypoxia by shifting the balance of signaling factors to stimulate the development of new blood vessels.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and metastatic monitoring
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biological stages, environmental dependencies, clinical tracking via circulating tumor cells, and genomic drivers involved in cancer dissemination.

topics.label: Summary and concluding remarks
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic reviews the core themes of the lecture and provides concluding advice on understanding cancer hallmark models.
